metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my friend's south indian restaurant called Kaveri Kitchen in Pune. people should be able to see the menu with prices, filter it by veg and non-veg, see today's specials, book a table on whatsapp, find the address and opening hours, see photos of the dishes, and read a few customer reviews. it should feel warm and homely and work well on phones

estimate_vs_charged.name: Page shell, warm styling, no-offer wording
Name, address, contacts and opening hours
Priced menu with veg and non-veg filter

review.verdict: A clean happy-path run: 7 workflows, all done, no conflicts, 0 failures, one audit pass, 120 of 200 spent, but it stressed almost none of J2's hard paths.

identity.note: Asked one bundled round of questions [2], got a full answer, recorded the charter, and closed with evidence [35]. The charter carries a garbled done-when item ('160... see menu price 180') and a rule the Requester never stated (editable data in one place). The low audit warning got no recorded disposition.

adaptation.note: One proposal covers all 12 done-when items and gives menu and specials one shared data object [8]. Seven workflows for a 38 KB page is more than the smallest useful split. The full proposal fields are not in the chat, so completeness is unverified.

priority.note: In role, no overreach. It granted all seven at once at the rate-card minimum [9] with no bargaining. The seven envelope checks are near-identical and 'Budget 120/200 used' never changes [12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30], so they show little judgment.

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule each time, ran W-1 first for the shell dependency and kept one writer on the lock [11, 14, 17]. The rule text is duplicated in [26] and [29]. Nothing was on hold, so HOLD handling went untested.

audit.note: Reported all 12 items passing [34], but its tally (18 PASS, 2 warnings) disagrees with the metrics (12 pass, 0 warnings). Filter results and the WhatsApp message content were judged 'on code', not in a browser. It did not flag the garbled charter item.

W-1.note: Shell and theme done [13]. The 'hide links to missing ids at load' rule can hide a missing section from the link check.

W-2.note: All contact facts match the charter [16]. Honest that it was not browser-run.

W-3.note: 11 dishes in one data object, filter counts by data 8 Veg and 3 Non-veg, matching the charter [19].

W-4.note: Specials read from the menu data, so Mysore dosa shows 180 and nothing is hard-coded [22].

W-5.note: Uses wa.me/910000033333 with the details in the message [25]. It added unrequested validation (past dates, time window), which is reasonable but beyond the declared scope.

W-6.note: Six labelled empty spots [28]. The 'real photos are coming' note is not a Requester-supplied fact.

W-7.note: Exactly the three supplied reviews and nothing extra [31].

went_well: Every agent stayed in role: 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator or role refusals.
One question round to the Requester was enough [2, 4]; nothing is left to be confirmed.
Menu and specials share one data object, so the filter and specials cannot drift apart [19, 22].
The code-run render check (360px, 1280px, JS errors, links) was clean [33].
No invented content: offers, prices and reviews match the Requester's facts.
problems: The charter's specials item contains leftover text '160... see menu price 180', and the validator still called the charter valid [7].
Audit's counts conflict: [34] says 18 PASS plus 2 warnings, metrics say 12 pass and 0 warnings. The Call us underline warning has no recorded outcome [34, 35].
No browser test of filtering or of the WhatsApp message contents; the only form check is 'submit' [33]. Builders said 'not yet run in a browser' [13 to 31].
Estimate equals charge for all 7 workflows, so cost is a rate-card figure, not a measurement.
Priority and Coordination envelope checks are templated and repeat 7 times for one tiny site [11 to 30].
learnings: This run tests only the happy path: 0 counters, refusals, conflicts, holds or retries, and 1 cycle. Next, set the budget below 120 or give a brief with a missing fact to exercise COUNTER/REFUSE and the Identity ruling.
Lessons memory was off (lessons.memory false), so the 'save a lesson' step is untested. Run a second cycle with memory on.
Add a charter check that rejects ellipses, unresolved text and figures that differ from the Requester's data. The 160/180 item got through.
Add scripted checks: click Veg and expect 8 dishes, Non-veg expect 3, submit the form and read the wa.me URL. Also confirm all six section ids exist, since W-1 hides links to missing ids [13].
Make Audit's tally match the metrics and require Identity to record what it did with each warning.

Log real model calls per workflow against the envelope. Today 'charged' equals the estimate, so Priority's scrutiny cannot be judged. Also test a 2 or 3 workflow split to see if the 14 overhead turns shrink; the cost is less isolation per section.

Keep: dependency-first scheduling with a stated rule, the single write lock, rate-card envelopes and the code-run render check. Evidence is thin on final page quality because I saw only messages and metrics, not the page.
